title: FancyZones (or perhaps some other component) disabled but seems to interfere with other app

judgment.rationale: The reporter already disabled the likely windowing group and tested exit, but the exact remaining enabled utilities and all-disabled result are missing.
evidence: The reporter uses 0.102.3101 on Windows 10 with AltSnap Win+drag across three screens; near a corner a border appears and drag sticks until Win is released.
Exiting PowerToys avoids the behavior; disabling most Windowing & Layouts utilities did not.

Grab and Move uses modifier capture and mouse hooks, but the report does not establish that it is enabled or responsible: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/237dc893c8c76b1bfa65994afda41ea7315a914c/src/modules/GrabAndMove/GrabAndMove/main.cpp.

proposed_fixes.title: Isolate the AltSnap screen-corner conflict
proposed_fixes.root_cause: A still-enabled utility or its interaction with AltSnap may be intercepting the gesture; neither FancyZones nor Grab and Move is established as the cause.
plan: Identify the enabled module or runner-only baseline using the reporter's all-disabled comparison.
Reproduce Win+drag at screen corners with that component and AltSnap, including a PowerToys-exited control.
Fix the verified input interaction and add a regression for the responsible gesture; retain normal edge behavior.
verification: AltSnap's Win+drag crosses the corner normally with the identified component active and no modifier remains stuck.

information_gaps.how_to_collect: Thanks for comparing with PowerToys exited and for disabling the Windowing & Layouts utilities. To isolate the remaining conflict, could you share which PowerToys utilities are still enabled, including any mouse utilities, and whether the same AltSnap drag works with all utilities disabled while PowerToys itself remains running? Please also identify which screen-edge utility, if any, draws the border. Your Windows version, AltSnap gesture, and admin setting are already in the report.
